// ---- catalog/index.mjs
// catalog: the toy's check catalogue, a legacy module first in the order (as BIO's legacy-checks).
export function checkList(list) {
  const findings = [];
  if (!Array.isArray(list)) {
    findings.push('not a list');
  }
  return findings;
}

// ---- alpha/src/index.mjs
// alpha: arithmetic for the dry run's toy product.

// The value as a message shows it: a string in quotes, anything else as written. Showing it never
// throws, whatever the value's getters or traps do, so the refusal stays a TypeError (R4, R5, R9).
function shown(x) {
  if (typeof x === 'string') return `'${x}'`;
  if (typeof x === 'bigint') return `${x}n`;
  if (typeof x === 'function') return '[function]';
  if (x === null || typeof x !== 'object') return String(x);
  try {
    return Array.isArray(x) ? JSON.stringify(x) : Object.prototype.toString.call(x);
  } catch {
    return '[object]';
  }
}

// `who: <place> is not a finite number: <value>`, the place counted from 1 (N2).
function finite(x, who, place) {
  if (typeof x !== 'number' || !Number.isFinite(x)) throw new TypeError(`${who}: ${place} is not a finite number: ${shown(x)}`);
  return x;
}

// R1, R5: a + b for finite numbers; anything else throws.
export function add(a, b) {
  return finite(a, 'add', 'argument 1') + finite(b, 'add', 'argument 2');
}

// R3–R4: left to right, 0 for an empty list; a non-finite element throws.
// Elements are checked, then added as `add` adds them. A running total that overflows to
// ±Infinity is carried on, not refused, since every element is finite (job record Q2).
export function sum(list) {
  let t = 0, i = 0;
  for (const x of list) t += finite(x, 'sum', `element ${++i}`);
  return t;
}

// R8–R9: left to right, 1 for an empty list (QUESTION #1: the identity of multiplication);
// a non-finite element throws, and a running total that overflows is carried on, as in `sum`.
export function product(list) {
  let t = 1, i = 0;
  for (const x of list) t *= finite(x, 'product', `element ${++i}`);
  return t;
}

// R10–R11: (a + b) / 2 rounded once. Where a + b is finite it is either exact (below 2^-1021, so the
// halving is the one rounding) or the halving is exact (above it). Where it overflows, both arguments
// are at least 2^971, so each half is exact and their sum is the one rounding.
export function midpoint(a, b) {
  const s = finite(a, 'midpoint', 'argument 1') + finite(b, 'midpoint', 'argument 2');
  return Number.isFinite(s) ? s / 2 : a / 2 + b / 2;
}

// ---- stats/src/index.mjs
// stats: statistics for the toy product; extracted from legacy (mean in D3, max and min in D4),
// and from catalog (distinct in D5).
import { sum } from '../../alpha/src/index.mjs';

// R1–R2: alpha.sum / length, 0 for an empty list; alpha.sum refuses a non-finite element.
export function mean(list) {
  const total = sum(list);
  return list.length ? total / list.length : 0;
}

// The extreme of a non-empty list of finite numbers, by a loop (no spread, so no argument limit).
// R8: an empty list is a RangeError first; an element that is not a finite number is a TypeError.
// `pick(x, m)` is Math.max or Math.min, so +0 and -0 come out as those give them.
function extreme(list, who, pick) {
  if (list.length === 0) throw new RangeError(`${who}: empty list`);
  let m;
  for (const x of list) {
    if (typeof x !== 'number' || !Number.isFinite(x)) throw new TypeError(`${who}: not a finite number: ${String(x)}`);
    m = m === undefined ? x : pick(x, m);
  }
  return m;
}

// R4–R5, R8: the largest number in a non-empty list; an empty list is a RangeError.
export function max(list) {
  return extreme(list, 'max', Math.max);
}

// R6–R7, R8: the smallest number in a non-empty list; an empty list is a RangeError.
export function min(list) {
  return extreme(list, 'min', Math.min);
}

// R9: true when no two elements are the same value as a Set compares them (SameValueZero), by one
// pass that stops at the first repeat; an empty list is distinct.
export function distinct(list) {
  const seen = new Set();
  for (const x of list) {
    if (seen.has(x)) return false;
    seen.add(x);
  }
  return true;
}

// R10–R11: the middle element of a stable sorted copy (the list is not changed; -0 and +0 keep their order) for an
// odd length. For an even length R11 asks alpha.midpoint of the two (A5), built in the completion round; until then
// alpha.sum of the two over 2. An empty list is a RangeError first, then an element
// that is not a finite number is a TypeError, as max refuses them (R5, R8).
export function median(list) {
  if (list.length === 0) throw new RangeError('median: empty list');
  for (const x of list) {
    if (typeof x !== 'number' || !Number.isFinite(x)) throw new TypeError(`median: not a finite number: ${String(x)}`);
  }
  const sorted = [...list].sort((a, b) => a - b);
  const mid = sorted.length >> 1;
  return sorted.length % 2 ? sorted[mid] : sum([sorted[mid - 1], sorted[mid]]) / 2;
}

// ---- legacy/index.mjs
// legacy: the toy's legacy module, emptied by extraction (PROCESS-MECHANICS §12).
import { checkList } from '../catalog/index.mjs';
import { distinct, max, min } from '../stats/src/index.mjs';

// The spread of a list: its largest element less its smallest.
export function range(list) {
  return max(list) - min(list);
}

// The findings the catalogue makes about a list, and 'duplicate' when a list's elements are not distinct.
export function validate(list) { return checkList(list).concat(Array.isArray(list) && !distinct(list) ? ['duplicate'] : []); }
